content: Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride, when co-administered with certain medications, can lead to increased toxicity or altered drug effects due to various mechanisms. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations for monitoring: 1. Mometasone Sinus Implant: Co-administration with magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride may increase toxicity. This is due to the potential for fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which can heighten the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Moxifloxacin (Oral): Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer moxifloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium to avoid chelation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 3. Nabumetone, Naproxen, and Oxaprozin: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, raising the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Neomycin (Oral): Increased toxicity may occur with co-administration. Monitor for adverse effects related to fluid and electrolyte disturbances. 5. Nilotinib: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride may increase nilotinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Nortriptyline, Olanzapine, and Paroxetine: These drugs may have enhanced central nervous system (CNS) depression when used with magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride. Monitor for signs of increased CNS depression and seizures, especially at higher magnesium doses. 7. Norfloxacin and Ofloxacin (Oral): Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases drug levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium to avoid chelation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Olmesartan, Telmisartan, and Valsartan: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, leading to seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Paliperidone, Pimavanserin, and Pimozide: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride may increase toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitor for cardiac arrhythmias and CNS depression. 10. Pancuronium, Rocuronium, and Vecuronium: Magnesium may potentiate the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents. Monitor for signs of enhanced neuromuscular blockade, such as muscle weakness or respiratory depression. 11. Panobinostat, Sotalol, and Vandetanib: Co-administration may increase toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider ECG monitoring in patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 12. Penicillamine (Oral): Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases penicillamine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer penicillamine at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium to avoid chelation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Prednisolone and Prednisone: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, heightening the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Primidone and Trimipramine: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride may increase the risk of seizures when used with drugs that lower the seizure threshold. Monitor closely for seizure activity. 15. Quetiapine, Thioridazine, and Ziprasidone: Co-administration may increase toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitor for cardiac arrhythmias and CNS depression. 16. Quinapril, Ramipril, and Trandolapril: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, leading to seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Risedronate, Alendronate, and Tiludronate: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Monitor for adverse effects. 18. Rifampin: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Samidorphan and Sertraline: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride may enhance CNS depression or increase the risk of seizures. Monitor closely for these effects. 20. Sevelamer and Sodium Polystyrene Sulfonate: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Streptomycin, Tobramycin, and Amikacin: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Monitor for renal impairment and other adverse effects. 22. Succinylcholine: Magnesium may potentiate the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents. Monitor for enhanced neuromuscular blockade. 23. Sucralfate and Sucroferric Oxyhydroxide: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Tetrabenazine and Vandetanib: Co-administration may increase toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider ECG monitoring in patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 25. Triamcinolone (Injectable): Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Trientine (Oral): Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases trientine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer trientine at least 1 hour before or after magnesium to avoid chelation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Zoledronic Acid: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Amiodarone and Vardenafil: Co-administration may increase toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Consider ECG monitoring in patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 29. Amphotericin B (All Forms): Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Amitriptyline and Amoxapine: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride may enhance CNS depression or increase the risk of seizures. Monitor closely for these effects. 31. Aluminum Hydroxide: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. In all cases, careful monitoring of the patient’s clinical status, including electrolyte levels, renal function, and cardiac rhythm, is essential to mitigate potential adverse effects.
